summary: DEF-019 foundation. Adds three read-only SECURITY DEFINER projections in public — cron job health, HTTP delivery health, and vault secret presence — because cron.job_run_details, net._http_response and vault.decrypted_secrets are unreadable by every party in this toolchain. Without them the DEF-018 evidence gate could never pass. No existing object is altered and nothing can write.

problem.trigger: The executor reported on 2026-08-05, while applying DEF-028, that cron.job_run_details and vault.decrypted_secrets are permission-denied to its psql role. The reviewing party's database connector exposes only the public schema and cannot reach them either.
problem.consequence_for_this_programme: The DEF-018 release declared post-apply checks that queried those relations directly. Those checks could never have passed — for anyone. Every delivery check would have errored and been recorded as a failure, and the release would have been permanently un-finalizable. A gate that cannot pass is worth no more than no gate at all, and worse: it looks like control.
problem.consequence_for_the_product: This same inaccessibility is why DEF-018 survived. 26,208 consecutive cron failures over seven days surfaced nowhere in the product, and no party in this toolchain could have looked even if they had thought to, because the table holding the evidence is unreadable by all of them. DEF-019 records that no alerting layer exists; this is its precondition. You cannot alert on what you cannot query.
problem.scope_note: This is the FOUNDATION for DEF-019, not its closure. It makes the failure surface queryable. It does not add alerting, thresholds, notification routing or a dashboard, and DEF-019 stays open until those exist.

design_decisions.decision: Follow the existing mcp_list_cron_jobs / mcp_list_functions wrapper pattern.
design_decisions.rationale: 20260722181057 already establishes the shape for this exact problem: a SECURITY DEFINER function in public exposing a narrowed, read-only projection of a catalog the caller cannot reach. Introducing a second mechanism for the same need would fragment the surface that DEF-015 had to sweep.

Those carry response bodies and echoed Authorization headers. The function needs to answer 'was the call accepted', which status codes and counts answer completely. Returning bodies would leak far more than delivery health to every authenticated staff user.

design_decisions.decision: Pass every free-text field through redact_secrets().
design_decisions.rationale: A failing net.http_post can echo its own bearer token into error_msg, and these projections are readable by all authenticated users. The redaction strips JWT-shaped strings and bearer/apikey/password/secret assignments. The migration asserts the redaction actually works against a real JWT shape before COMMIT, so it cannot ship as a comment that does nothing.

design_decisions.decision: mcp_vault_secret_present returns a boolean, never a value.
design_decisions.rationale: The executor could not perform the one pre-check DEF-018 depends on — that email_queue_service_role_key exists and is non-empty — because the vault is entirely unreadable to it. Presence is the question; the value is never the answer, so the function is shaped so it cannot be coerced into returning one.
If the function owner cannot read the vault either, returning false would read as 'the secret is absent' and could send someone to create a duplicate secret. It raises instead, naming the failure.

design_decisions.decision: Report rather than raise when net._http_response is absent.
design_decisions.rationale: pg_net's response relation is internal and has been renamed across versions. Returning {available: false, reason} lets a verifier check fail with a legible cause instead of an opaque relation-does-not-exist error.

design_decisions.decision: LEFT JOIN cron.job_run_details so every job appears even with zero runs.
design_decisions.rationale: A job that is scheduled but never firing is the failure mode that matters most, and an inner join would hide it by omission — the row would simply not be there. runs = 0 is visible; an absent row is not.

design_decisions.decision: Surface unrecognized_parameter_failures as its own count.
design_decisions.rationale: That is the DEF-018 signature exactly. Making it a first-class column means a regression is unmistakable rather than something to be inferred by reading error strings.

design_decisions.decision: Revoke from PUBLIC and anon on all four functions, and assert it before COMMIT.
design_decisions.rationale: DEF-015 closed 90 SECURITY DEFINER functions that were anon-executable because the default PUBLIC grant was never revoked — including one introduced by this programme's own earlier work. The post-assertions check has_function_privilege for anon, authenticated and service_role on every function created here, and check that search_path is pinned (DEF-005), so this release cannot reintroduce either defect.

expected_objects.object: redact_secrets, mcp_cron_job_health, mcp_http_delivery_health and mcp_vault_secret_present all exist in public
anon holds EXECUTE on none of the four; authenticated and service_role hold it on all four
expected_objects.verify_via: has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') = false for each; true for authenticated and service_role. Asserted in-migration, but re-check live per DEF-015.

expected_objects.object: Every SECURITY DEFINER function created here has a pinned search_path
expected_objects.verify_via: catalog_functions — assert search_path is non-null on each (DEF-005)

expected_objects.object: mcp_cron_job_health(20) returns one row per cron job, including jobs with zero runs
expected_objects.verify_via: SELECT jsonb_array_length(public.mcp_cron_job_health(20)) — expect it to equal the count from cron.job (13 after DEF-018 applies, 12 before)
SELECT public.mcp_http_delivery_health(20)->>'available' — expect true. If false, net._http_response is named differently in this pg_net version and the DEF-018 delivery checks cannot run.

SELECT public.mcp_vault_secret_present('email_queue_service_role_key'). TRUE unblocks DEF-018. FALSE means the secret must be set before DEF-018 is applied. An exception means the vault is unreadable even to the function owner, which is a separate problem to raise.
SELECT public.redact_secrets('Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ4In0.sig') — must not contain 'eyJhbGci'. Asserted in-migration too.

post_publish_verification.gate_policy: Convention section 3. Every check must pass before this release may move out of pending/.

checks.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND proname IN ('redact_secrets','mcp_cron_job_health','mcp_http_delivery_health','mcp_vault_secret_present')

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND proname IN ('redact_secrets','mcp_cron_job_health','mcp_http_delivery_health','mcp_vault_secret_present') AND has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE')

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND proname IN ('redact_secrets','mcp_cron_job_health','mcp_http_delivery_health','mcp_vault_secret_present') AND has_function_privilege('authenticated', oid, 'EXECUTE')

SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc p WHERE p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND p.proname IN ('mcp_cron_job_health','mcp_http_delivery_health','mcp_vault_secret_present') AND p.prosecdef AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(coalesce(p.proconfig, ARRAY[]::text[])) cfg WHERE cfg LIKE 'search_path=%')
SELECT CASE WHEN (public.mcp_http_delivery_health(20)->>'available')::boolean THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
SELECT CASE WHEN public.redact_secrets('Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ4In0.sig') LIKE '%eyJhbGci%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

steps: Apply FIRST, before 20260805100000 (DEF-018). It is read-only, alters no existing object, and the DEF-018 evidence gate depends on the projections it adds.

Apply 20260805160000_def_019_cron_and_delivery_observability.sql. Self-verifying: post-assertions abort if any function is missing, if anon holds EXECUTE on any of them, if authenticated or service_role lack it, if a SECURITY DEFINER function has no pinned search_path, if either health function fails to answer, or if the JWT redaction does not strip a real JWT shape.
Immediately run: SELECT public.mcp_vault_secret_present('email_queue_service_role_key'); — this is the DEF-018 prerequisite you could not previously check. Report the result before applying DEF-018.

Run: SELECT public.mcp_cron_job_health(20); and paste the raw output. This is the first time the 26,208-failure signature has been queryable, and the six GUC jobs should show non-zero unrecognized_parameter_failures until DEF-018 is applied — which is itself the pre-apply reproduction for that release.
Report the executor's applied version so it can be recorded in docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json.

guarded_by: src/test/regression/def-019-observability.test.ts — static guards over the migration, including that no function returns response content or headers, that all four revoke anon, that redaction is asserted in-migration rather than merely defined, and that the cron projection uses a LEFT JOIN so a never-firing job is visible rather than absent.

live_apply.note: All four functions created; the migration's own post-assertion block PERFORMed mcp_cron_job_health(20) and mcp_http_delivery_health(20) successfully before COMMIT, so both answer when called by a role that holds EXECUTE. mcp_vault_secret_present was NOT exercised by the post-assertions and remains unproven.

limitation: STATICALLY VALIDATED ONLY — this migration has not been executed against Postgres. It is wrapped in a single transaction and will roll back cleanly on error. The `net._http_response` reference is guarded by to_regclass and executed dynamically, so a pg_net version that names the relation differently degrades to available=false rather than failing the migration.

managed database connector — connects as supabase_read_only_user. Same 42501.
PostgREST as a real authenticated user — no usable test credential; portal-b-qa@accountancyos.test sign-in failed.
executor_blocker.not_caused_by_def_031: rolbypassrls bypasses row security, not privilege checks. These denials are ACL, and would have occurred identically before DEF-031.
executor_blocker.same_class_as_the_defect_def_019_fixes: The gate still cannot pass for the party required to run it — the reason has moved from schema USAGE on cron to EXECUTE on the projections.
executor_blocker.remedy_not_taken: No grant added. Owner ruling point 3.
executor_blocker.consequence: DEF-018 is HELD. Its mandatory pre-check — mcp_vault_secret_present('email_queue_service_role_key') — cannot be performed by the executor.
